channel.title: Acme: Light News
channel.description: Positive, lighthearted and unusual current news.

item.title: Kerala rescue saves more than 19,500 orchids from roadwork
item.description: Researchers moved 27,324 orchids from trees threatened by road construction in southern India to a beach and two urban wetlands. After 12 to 24 months, nearly 71% were still alive; many flowered and produced seed, turning an emergency rescue into a promising conservation model.

item.title: A shy shelter dog finds the patient home she needed
item.description: Alena, a terrier mix whose kennel anxiety discouraged adopters, found a home six days after an online feature showed her relaxed foster-care personality. Her new family had experience with timid dogs and gives her space to approach on her own terms; the shelter calls it a perfect match.

item.title: Beaver family returns to the Loch Ness watershed after 500 years
item.description: A family of six beavers was released Nov. 4 at the Dundreggan rewilding estate, the first recorded return to the Loch Ness catchment since the species was hunted to extinction in Scotland. The project plans to restore at least 15 family groups across the watershed over three years.

item.title: Rehabilitated bald eagle takes flight over North Carolina Zoo
item.description: A four-year-old female bald eagle found barely responsive at a landfill in September returned to the wild after nearly two months of care. Her Nov. 4 flight over the North Carolina Zoo's lake also marked the 25th anniversary of its wildlife rehabilitation center.

item.title: Volunteers plant nearly 500 pines in New Mexico burn scar
item.description: Volunteers, the Rocky Mountain Youth Corps and the Los Vigiles Land Grant have planted nearly 500 ponderosa pine seedlings in the Hermit's Peak-Calf Canyon burn area since October. Crews hope to put another 500 in the ground before winter.

item.title: Georgia eighth-grader wins cheer competition as a squad of one
item.description: When the rest of her squad dropped out, eighth-grader Jorgia Walls performed alone at a Georgia cheer competition. She completed the routine before hundreds of spectators and won first place, turning an unexpected setback into an exuberant solo victory.

item.title: Students build a 300-drone wish for a Colorado boy
item.description: St. Vrain Valley high school students created a custom drone-light show for Nathaniel “Bubba” Brown, a Make-A-Wish recipient who loves lights. The student-run team designed the aerial animations, music and flight plan, turning the Holyoke sky into a colorful celebration for Bubba and his family.

item.title: Three inventors recall how two jockstraps became the sports bra
item.description: Lisa Lindahl, Polly Smith and Hinda Miller turned a 1977 joke about a women's jockstrap into the Jogbra. Their seamless prototype arrived as Title IX expanded women's sports, grew into a billion-dollar product category and earned the trio induction into the National Inventors Hall of Fame.

item.title: Rugby gives a young U.S. Olympian a place to belong
item.description: Fifteen-year-old Eseta Moala says rugby transformed the size that once made sports clothes uncomfortable into a source of strength. Inspired by U.S. star Ilona Maher, Moala joined her sister Luisa on the American rugby sevens team at the Youth Olympics in Dakar—and received a personal video from Maher.

item.title: Drone delivers bananas to chimp cut off by Florida floods
item.description: Flooded roads at Save the Chimps near Fort Pierce prevented staff from reaching 38-year-old Kaleb, so caregivers sent food and blankets by drone. Video showed him taking a banana from the dropped bag before crossing standing water on a rope. All 200 sanctuary chimps stayed safe and fed.

item.title: Tiny transmitters reveal the monarch butterfly's epic migration
item.description: Scientists and community volunteers are fitting monarch butterflies with solar-powered transmitters weighing about as much as a grain of rice. The tags let researchers and the public follow individual insects on journeys of up to 3,000 miles to Mexico through the free Project Monarch Science app.

item.title: Empire Life's 57-year United Way tradition sets a record
item.description: Empire Life employees and retirees raised a record C$304,018 for United Way programs across Canada, exceeding a C$270,000 goal. The insurer matched pledges up to C$125,000. It was the campaign's tenth straight year above target and the highest total in the company's 57 years of annual drives.

item.title: Giant pandas return to Zoo Atlanta
item.description: Zoo Atlanta introduced six-year-old giant pandas Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, whose names mean peace and double happiness. The pair arrived after a two-year panda gap and made their public debut in a renovated habitat, renewing a long-running conservation partnership with China.

item.title: Previously unknown right whale calf spotted in Canada
item.description: Researchers confirmed a previously unknown North Atlantic right whale calf after a September 25 sighting near Anticosti Island. Its mother is 38-year-old Silt, and the calf is her sixth. The discovery raises the season total to 24, the fourth-highest on record for a species numbering about 380.

item.title: A$25 million gift will expand Australian wildlife conservation
item.description: The Wright Burt Foundation pledged A$25 million to Australian Wildlife Conservancy, part of a A$120 million commitment to 10 organizations. The gift will support land purchases, feral-cat control and threatened-species recovery as AWC works to influence conservation across more than 5% of Australia by 2035.
